articleTitle: Unidirectional line-focusing shear vertical wave EMATs used for rail base center flaw detection
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT) is used for rail base flaw detection. The bidirectional radiation pattern of Shear Vertical wave (SV-wave) EMAT limits the accuracy and efficiency of the transducers. In view of this problem, a method of generating unidirectional focusing SV wave is brought up by a unidirectional line-focusing SV-wave EMAT. A 2D finite element model is built to demonstrate the feasibility of rail base flaw detection. Finally, the unidirectional line-focusing SV-wave EMAT is compared experimentally with other three kinds of SV-wave EMATs. The results show that using the unidirectional SV-wave EMAT can enhance the amplitude of echo signal into around two times of the bidirectional EMAT. Compared with bidirectional SV-wave EMAT and unidirectional SV-wave EMAT, the amplitude of echo signals are increased by 7% and by 10% by line-focusing SV-wave EMAT and unidirectional line-focusing SV wave EMAT, respectively.

articleTitle: Rail inspection research based on high speed phased array ultrasonic technology
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Rail is one of the vital components of the railway system. Rail flaw detection plays an important role in ensuring the safety of railway transportation. Nowadays, rail inspection system based on conventional ultrasonic technology can't meet the practical application needs well due to the problems of low-detection coverage rate and inconvenient to change ultrasonic angle. To solve those problems, a high speed phased array ultrasonic technology is proposed for rail inspection. By utilizing this phased array technology, rail inspection speed can be improved to 100Km/h, with the character of better ultrasonic coverage and convenient to change ultrasonic angle without replacing probe. In summary, high speed phased array technology can meet the inspection demands of high speed, high efficiency, and high coverage in Chinese rail inspection.

articleTitle: Research on rail defect detection system based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The paper describes the design of a rail defect detection system, which is suitable for 43 kg/m to 75 kg/m rails' in service inspection requirements. The defect acquisition module of the system is composed of some conventional probes and phased array probes. In defect signal processing module, FPGA was used to deal with the multi-channel defect data by using its parallel processing function. The system has the advantages of high detection accuracy, high detection rate, etc., 60kg/m rail detection accuracy of up to 6mm, the highest detection rate of up to 90km/h, with a certain practical value.

articleTitle: Emissivity correction of eddy current pulsed thermography for rail inspection
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Eddy current pulsed thermography (ECPT) is an emerging non-destructive testing and evaluation (NDT&E) technique for conductive material. However, surface emissivity variation of metallic object influences accurate temperature mapping in infrared thermography, which leads to false alarm of defect detection. This paper proposes a new emissivity correction method for ECPT based on spectral reflectance measurement in infrared and visible wavelengths. A graphical indicator was calculated based on normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) algorithm and utilized for reducing the influence of emissivity variation. Experimental studies were conducted on steel plate and rail samples with different calibrated emissivity to verify its capability for artificial and natural rail cracks characterization. Results demonstrated this method can effectively improve defect detectability of ECPT for rail inspection.

articleTitle: Identifying lack of fusion defects in high-density polyethylene piping welds
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, microwave testing technique for identifying lack of fusion defects in thermal fusion weld of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipeline is proposed. HDPE piping thermal fusion welds with lack of fusion defects of different degrees were examined using a vector network analyzer and a self-designed microwave measuring system with a success. At a frequency that was most sensitive to the lack of fusion defects, the measured reflection coefficient S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) had significantly different values between the good weld and those containing lack of fusion defects. The readily detectable differences in S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and VSWR make identification of the lack of fusion defects possible. True density experiment and scan electron microscopy were conducted to confirm the reliability of the microwave testing methods. This work provides great insights into inspection of technical defects in HDPE piping welds.

articleTitle: Impact damage detection and characterization using eddy current pulsed thermography
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Reciprocating impact load leads to plastic deformation of the metal, which will cause fatigue and cracks. Due to the complex surface condition and various types of damage, it is difficult to extract the feature of nature micro cracks by using common thermograph NDT methods. This paper presents the feasibility study of using eddy current pulse thermography for detecting impact damages of torque arm in aircraft brake system. The optical flow algorithm is used to characterize the thermal diffusion and extract the transient thermal behavior among impact areas under the complex background noise. In addition, the spatial-transient pattern analysis is hybrid to automatically detect the nature cracks. Experiment study has been conducted and the magnetic particle is presented to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of synchronous projection data acquisition system for cone beam CT based on manipulator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to satisfy the requirement of automatic nondestructive testing of micro defects for the casting and forging components whose shape and curvature are complex (such as aircraft engine blades), we develop a CT testing system based on six degrees of freedom industrial manipulator using computerized tomography scan of detection method. The measurement system is mainly composed of three major parts: manipulator, flat panel detector and high energy X-ray source. We carry out further analysis for the purpose of the coordinated control system and the overall design scheme based on the analysis of the basic composition and working mechanism of each unit introduced in this paper. To meet the data synchronization acquisition in every angle for the testing work piece, we design the bottom program, hardware circuit and host program to realize coordination and orderly operation of the whole detection system based on the analysis above.

articleTitle: Research on phased array ultrasonic technique for testing butt fusion joint in polyethylene pipe
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) pipe has been widely used for the transportation of gas in cities because of the excellent corrosion resistance, good mechanical properties, excellent welding performance and longer service life. Fusion welding is one of the main connection methods of polyethylene pipe. However, the defects in butt fusion joints due to circumstances and wrong operation are very common on the work site, which have been one of the most serious risks of pipeline system. On the base of the classification of defects in PE butt fusion joint, the phased array ultrasonic technique is presented, with the purpose of overcoming the detecting difficulty caused by the attenuation of PE. An automatic ultrasonic testing system is designed and fabricated. The reliability and process performance are tested through detecting PE butt fusion joints with typical defects. It is shown that the ultrasonic techniques presented in the paper are applicable for the detecting of typical defects such as pores, inclusions on fusion surface and lack of fusion in PE joints, which will improve the safety of PE pipeline.

articleTitle: Excitation power design base on series resonant electromagnetic ultrasonic sensor for pipeline NDT
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: EMAT is an emerging non-destructive testing technique which has been applied to the pipelines monitoring. It has advantages of non coupling agent and can be used in high temperature, high accuracy as well as wide range detection. High energy consumption and low conversion efficiency are two main challenges for NDT by using EMAT. This paper proposes a new pipeline electromagnetic ultrasonic excitation power and transducer design based on series resonant EMAT sensor. The specific contents include: (i) Electromagnetic acoustic transducer energy transfer principle analysis. (ii) Series resonant structure EMAT sensors design and energy analysis. Simulation have been conducted and the validation results of the proposed structure that provide an effective method to verify the new design of excitation power for EMAT pipeline NDT.

articleTitle: Experimental study of turbine disk residual stress measurement using Lcr wave
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Turbine disk usually cracks near the arc junction between the rim and the plate (called the root of turbine disk). This paper presents the application of an ultrasonic method to measure stresses on the root of turbine disk. The ultrasonic residual stresses measurement is based on the acoustoelastic effect that refers to the change in velocity of the elastic wave when propagating in a stressed media. We employ critically refracted longitudinal waves(Lcr wave) and relate its time variation with applied stress. This paper studies the propagation law of Lcr wave in inclined surface of different angles and verifies that Lcr wave can propagate on rectangular components. The specific probe head is designed to detect residual stress on the root of the turbine disk. The experimental result shows that it is feasible to use Lcr wave to detect residual stress on the roots of the turbine disk.

articleTitle: Inspection and treatment for surface cracks of stainless steel surfacing layer in pressurized hydrogen environment
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Stainless steel surfacing layer is widely used for the equipments working in pressurized hydrogen environment such as hydrogenation reactors in order to improve the corrosion resistance. Surface cracking is a basic failure mode of the layer due to the extreme working condition. It is also a quite difficult problem for safety assessment and defect elimination. In this paper, a typical case of surface cracking of the layer in hydrogen environment is analyzed in detail. Inspection methods including non-destructive testing (NDT) for confirming quantity and location of surface cracks are introduced. Surface cracking causes and treatment methods for the defects are also studied. Finally, some suggestions for inspection and treatment of surface cracks of the layer are proposed. Phased array ultrasonic testing is an effective NDT method for confirming the extension of surface cracks. Fitness for service assessment for the cracks of stainless steel surfacing layer is suggested. Defect elimination method is only suggested to be adopted if the cracks extend into the base metal.

articleTitle: Revealing the stresses — New approach for industrial safety, reliability and residual life assessment
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Today's technology demands higher emphasis on safety of industrial components, accurate measurements with intelligent prognosis on condition monitoring, reliable residual life assessment and life extension techniques. This presentation highlights a new approach for industrial safety by using innovative device, the Indicator of Mechanical Stresses (IMS). The main goal is to estimate the safety of operation and to monitor the condition, the remaining operational life of the structure and to draw conclusions based on the practical results of the structure in question, mainly from ferromagnetic steel.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of austenitic stainless steel weld defect detection in ultrasonic phased array based on DORT
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: For weld in thick walled austenitic stainless steel welds inspection, it is difficult to develop a spatial imaging algorithm for accurate defect detection. The traditional DORT algorithm cannot be used in many commercial ultrasonic phased array detectors, because it requires one element in the probe transmitted a pulse and all elements received echo signals. Many commercial probes can transmit and receive signals using the same number elements. The improved DORT was proposed to suitable for multiple elements transmitting signal and multiple elements receiving echo. The relative performance of the improved DORT algorithm is illustrated using simulated and experimental data. Various manufactured flaws (side-drilled holes of 2 mm diameter) have been machined at several depths of austenitic stainless steel weld block. Despite the high backscattering noise due to multiple scattering, a significant improvement of the detection performances is observed.

articleTitle: A multi-source information fusion approach for crack detection of 42CrMo steel during fatigue test
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: For non-destructive testing (NDT) to be applicable in mechanical equipment, it is mandatory that NDT is highly flexible, accurate and robust. At present there have been several methods based on acoustic, optical and electromagnetic information to detect the cracks of the mechanical equipment. As a new technology, the fusion of testing information harnesses the advantages of various NDT instruments, and thus improve the accuracy of the result. In this paper, a multi-source information fusion approach for the cracks of 42CrMo steel is presented. First, we collect the information from the acoustic emission, machine vision and infrared instruments. Second, we take advantage of the software Matlab to build a fusion model, which can enhance the relationship of the detective information to increase the crack's recognition rate greatly. Finally, we analyze the cracks' location and length based on the result of the model. We evaluate the proposed fusion model, and the experiment shows that the fusion result achieves a better performance than single testing.

articleTitle: Massive multi-frequency excitation and spectrogram eddy current method for defects identification in clad materials
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The paper presents a measurement system for a massive multi-frequency excitation and a spectrogram eddy current inspection. The systems offers a high sensitivity and a very good depth resolution. It is especially useful in case of clad materials' inspection due to availability of information from different depths. It is achieved by using many excitation frequencies at the same time. Additionally, the spectrogram, which is a two-dimensional display of relative amplitudes of frequency components of a signal from a pick-up coil versus a sensor position, enables easy way to identify location of a defect as well as it's parameters.

articleTitle: A calibration method of workpiece frames for ultrasonic testing using twin-robot
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: A calibration method of workpiece frames using twin-robot is presented in this paper. Path planning for workpiece is based on its frame. Thus, the workpiece frames of two robots should be calibrated to make sure the motion of the twin-robot is under the same coordinate system. However, when twin-robot are separated from the workpiece, the twin-robot cannot reach some calibration points on workpiece at the same time. So a new method is proposed to solve the problem. The translation and rotation matrices between the base frames of two robots can be obtained by measuring the coordinate values of any three non-collinear points in working space. When only one robot can actually reach the calibration point of the workpiece frame, the coordinate value of this point in another robot base frame can be obtained by the matrices calculation. Experiment results show that the calibration method is relatively precision and convenient.

articleTitle: Acoustic emission characteristic of 42CrMo material in the process of tension
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The steel of 42CrMo is regarded as a structural material in crankshaft, due to the significant advantages they offer, such as high strength, high toughness and good temper brittleness. So the investigation of tensile properties of 42CrMo is important to prevent failure. The acoustic emission (AE) technique was widely used in monitoring the process of failure and it has function of early warning. In this paper, the AE technique was used to monitor the process of tensile test and the characteristics of AE parameters and spectrum were extracted. Which have obvious significance to study the features of different stages of process of tensile.

articleTitle: Quality control of in-service inspection in nuclear island
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: During the refueling outages of PWRs, ISI in nuclear island will contribute to find the equipment degradation generated during its normal operation, which can lay a foundation for the safe operation of nuclear power plant. ISI of nuclear island equipment was carried out from two sides: implementation and management. A detailed process of nondestructive testing and quality control during the preparation stage, project implementation stage and postsession integration stage was presented in accordance with the project procedures. Main responsibilities of quality control personnel stand out in the whole process.

articleTitle: Design of NDT robot control system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The development of automated NDT is more and more fast, in order to better serve the needs of NDT, we independently research robot system facing to the test, and achieve it's preliminary application. Basing on MOTOMAN-MH6 six degrees of freedom robot, this paper sets up “computer + PMAC + manipulation motor” motion control system, achieves to three closed-loop system in order to meet the exact requirements of the position control. Basing on D-H parameters, we set up robot coordinate system and kinematics model, research and write algorithm which is in line with the guidelines applicable to pieper six degrees of freedom serial robot. In addition to this, we call Pcommserver and Opencascade dynamic link library to design and write “motion control + motion simulation” interface in the host computer, which can meet the needs of human-computer interaction. Finally, the robot system facing to the testing is applied to parts of the NDT projects, and is preliminary proved it's feasibility and reliability.

articleTitle: High reliable unilateral inductive axle counting sensor system and applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This paper proposes a new high reliable unilateral inductive axle counting sensor prototype based on eddy-current principle. It could send out strong analog signal several kilometers away without any trackside or inner magnifying circuits because of its special open flux magnetic structure and signal processing method. The operational principle of the sensor is studied with modeling as well as the validation by experiments in labs. Signal processing is implemented to extract the information of train's occupation including the vehicle speed, traversing direction, wheel diameter and so on. It also conforms to the requirement of the Safety Integrity Level 3 standard. The performance of this proposed sensor is discussed with different operational conditions for the future work.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation into probability of detection for fatigue cracks in sonic IR imaging
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Probability of detection (POD) for defects under given test conditions is an important statistical technique for the detection reliability assessment. In this study, we investigate a set of 45 steel specimens with fatigue cracks in different lengths. Experimental results show that the increase of the crack length will enhance the crack heating response, and the logarithmic relationship between the response signal and the crack length has a better linearity compared to others. Based on experimental data and the statistic characteristics, the linear regression analysis is introduced to estimate the POD function. The study provides a quantitative evaluation for the crack detection reliability in sonic infrared imaging.

articleTitle: Quantitative imaging of thickness maps using ultrasonic guided wave tomography based on full-waveform inversion
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: An ultrasonic guided wave tomography method based on full waveform inversion (FWI) is developed for high resolution and accurate reconstructions of the remaining wall thickness in isotropic plates. The inversion is based on local optimization of the waveform misfit function between modeled and measured data. The modeled data is computed in the frequency domain implementing a full-wave equation using Finite Difference (FD) method, accounting for higher order effects such as diffractions and multiple scattering. Experiments were carried out to measure the dispersive guided wave propagating through different types of defects. The inversion is applied iteratively to discrete frequency components from low to high frequencies. The resulting wave velocity maps are then converted to thickness maps by the dispersion characteristics of selected guided modes. The experimental results show that the FWI algorithm can achieve accurate reconstructions with the thickness error less than 1 mm on a 10 mm thick plate.

articleTitle: Application of acoustic emission technology in the main primary system hydraulic proof test for EPR nuclear reactors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This article introduced the basic principle of acoustic emission technology and its characteristics. It summarized the applications of acoustic emission technology in leakage monitoring for the reactor vessel closure head and pressurizer bottom head penetrations where are inaccessible during the main primary system hydraulic proof test for EPR nuclear reactors. It provided reference for the acoustic emission technology in leakage monitoring for the third generation nuclear reactors in China.

articleTitle: Focal law design for phased array ultrasonic testing of CFRP based on finite element modeling
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The focal law of linear phased array ultrasonic testing of carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) laminates was studied based on finite element modeling. Two stacking sequences, [0]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</sub> and [45/90/-45/0]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>, were considered and the focusing results were compared based on the calculation of transient acoustic field. It was found that the actual focal point was ahead of the preset location when the focal law was calculated with a constant velocity of 2980 m/s, and the focal depth of [0]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</sub> laminate was much smaller than that of [45/90/-45/0]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>. To realize the focal law design, the time delay from each element to the preset focal point was acquired based on the finite element simulation and the focusing was obviously improved. The results were also verified by experiments. The differences were comprehensively discussed based on the wave propagation behavior in the elastic anisotropy and laminar structure.

articleTitle: Research on automatic TV inspection technology of steam generator secondary side center lane
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Based on the television inspection requirement of steam generator secondary side center lane, the center lane automatic TV inspection technology was studied and inspection device was developed. In this paper, the mechanism, components and results of inspection device were described. By far, such a device has already been successfully applied to NPP domestic.

articleTitle: The frequency dependence of ultrasonic attenuation in water
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The amplitude of ultrasonic will occur some attenuation when it traveled in liquids. And the ultrasonic attenuation with different frequency in the liquid is not same. In this paper, two experiments are designed to research how the amplitude of the ultrasonic will change with different frequencies of ultrasonic traveling in the water. And we find that the ultrasonic attenuation with different frequency in the water is not same, and the higher the frequency, the higher the multiple of attenuation. This conclusion has great significance in the field of high-frequency ultrasound.

articleTitle: Thickness and surface flaws detection using EMAT&ECT for medium plate rolling in intermediate cooling process
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: It is significant for improving the quality of medium plate to detect the thickness and surface flaws in intermediate cooling process in real time. A novel EMAT&ECT fusion method is proposed to realize three dimensional (3D) imaging for the surface flaws and thickness of medium plate in this paper. EMAT is used for the medium plate thickness measurement, and ECT for surface defects detection. We designed a scanning method for 3D imaging of medium plate, which combines EMAT and ECT. At the same time, the 3D imaging principle of EMAT&ECT fusion testing method is introduced. Results by simulation and experiments showed that the method is feasible using EMAT&ECT for medium plate quality detection in intermediate cooling process.

articleTitle: Investigation of eddy current signals on steam generator tube anti-vibration bars
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Steam generator tubes has anti-vibration bars in U-bend area for supporting tubes and avoiding unacceptable flow induced vibration or micro vibration induced wear. This article describes anti-vibration bar shift of 55/19B model steam generator and using eddy current inspection to investigate the respective anti-vibration bar shift signal and the gap between tube and anti-vibration bar.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of debonding NDT for multi-layer metal-metal bonding structure by using eddy current pulsed thermography
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Multi-layer metal-metal bonding structure is widely applied in aviation, aerospace, and nuclear industrial fields. Debonding defects retains high attention in Nondestructive testing and evaluation society. This paper proposes the feasibility study for inner debonding defect detection of lead-steel bonding structure by using eddy current pulsed thermography. Numerical study has been conducted for validation and the studies on detectability sensitivity curve versus effect of excitation current and heating time are reported. According to the numerical study, detection sensitivity and excitation current are monotonic related, and the optimum heating time is identified.

articleTitle: EFPI sensor time division multiplexing technology using reflective semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: An extrinsic Fabry-Perot interferometrie (EFPI) optical fiber sensor interrogation system using reflective semiconductor optical amplifier (RSOA) is proposed. In this novel design, a resonant cavity is formed between the RSOA and EFPI sensors, each sensor can access to by tuning the modulation frequency of RSOA. Compared with common EFPI sensor interrogator, this design allows tens of sensors along a single optical fiber. Results demonstrated the signal have good SNR without measurable crosstalk between sensors.

articleTitle: Research of SNR enhancement for coarse-grained CASS based on phase coherence imaging
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The cast austenitic stainless steel (CASS) is hard to be detected using general ultrasonic methods on account of the low signal to noise ratio (SNR) caused by coarse-grained structure. A numerical model based on electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD) was established to simulate the phased array ultrasonic imaging of CASS. Aiming to enhance SNR, the phase coherence imaging (PCI) technique was implemented to process total focusing method (TFM) image. The phase coherence factors which represented the phase dispersion for each pixel were established and the amplitudes of structural noise in original TFM image with high phase diversity were effectively suppressed by phase coherence weighting. Numerical calculation results show that the SNR values of Φ3 side drilled hole with 50mm depth in 96 mm thickness CASS model are more than 30dB in TFM-PCI images. Comparing to original TFM image, the SNR increments are over 10dB.

articleTitle: The influence of notch characteristics on magnetic memory signals
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: For studying the influence of notch characteristics on magnetic memory signals, static tension tests on Q235 steel were carried out. The normal component of magnetic flux leakage, Hp(y), were measured by metal magnetic memory testing, and the relationship between the magnetic field values at a fixed point with stress under different loads were studied; carrying ANSYS simulation on double associated notch specimen, and studying the internal stress distribution of double associated notch specimen and the relationship between the magnetic field value at a fixed point with stress; comparing the experimental results with simulation results and found that test results is consistent with the simulation results. The results show that semicircular notch is more potential danger than V-shaped notch specimen; magnetic field values at the center of notch of the double associated notch specimen is approximately superimposed on single notch specimen magnetic field values in corresponding position. The normal component of magnetic flux leakage Hp(y) and gradient value k(y) in stress concentration of double associated notch specimen are no longer applicable of evaluating stress concentration degree of double associated notch.

articleTitle: Inspection of nonconductive coatings using time domain terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper the possibility of using a terahertz (THz) electromagnetic waves for detection of coatings' defects was investigated. In the last years, terahertz spectroscopy has gained more interest because of its unique capabilities. THz radiation lies above the frequency range of traditional radio and microwaves but below the range of infrared waves. The THz radiation allows achieving a very good spatial resolution and penetration depth. Moreover, THz inspection has the potential for a higher resolution than ultrasound due to its shorter wavelength. A set of experiments was carried out and the achieved results prove usability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Surface acoustic wave propagation in the variable-thickness complex shape components
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Variable-thickness curved components, that have been widely used in many fields, are always caused serious accidents by the surface and subsurface defects, Therefore, how to detect and identify the variable-thickness complex shape components defects is of great significance. For the variable-thickness shape components' surface and sub-surface defects' detecting, it has been testified that surface wave detecting theory is correct by analyzing the effects of curvature radius to the surface wave's velocity and wave number theoretically. Based on the theoretical analysis conclusions and the wavelet signal processing method, a synthetically defect location identification method has been presented. Finally, the defect orientation identification has been researched more accurately with the principle of ellipse imaging algorithm. The experimental results show that the surface wave detecting method could detect the location, depth and orientation of defect in the variable-thickness complex shape components accurately.

articleTitle: Recent advances in ultrasonic volume visualization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Volume Visualization is a technique for demonstrating the object inside information in three dimensions, which has a good supporting role in ultrasonic testing. The research of ultrasound volume visualization is more focused on the medical field than on industrial field. This paper has summarized the recent advances in ultrasound volume visualization technology, including the classification and pre-processing of volume data, the algorithms of three-dimensional volume rendering, and analyzed the key technique of volume visualization in industrial ultrasound. The research of ultrasonic volume visualization on industrial will become a hot spot, with the non-destructive testing increasingly demanding in recent year, especially in the requirements of quantitative non-destructive testing.

articleTitle: Simulation and experiment study of non-destructive testing using EMA/EC dual probe
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: It is of some advantages for non-destructive testing surface and internal flaws using EC/EMA dual probe. The fusion detection principle of EMA/EC is emulated by finite element method. Aimed to EC, the current eddy field distribution focused on skin and coil impedance variation induced by eddy field is studied by theory and experiment method, and aimed to EMAT, the propagation characteristics of the ultrasonic wave excited by EMAT is analyzed by Multiphysics Comsol simulation software. The simulation and experiment results showed that it is effective methods for non-destructive testing surface and internal flaw of the tested object using EC/EMA fusion detection method.

articleTitle: Localization and evaluation of subsurface pits in copper pipes using gradient-field pulsed eddy current inspection
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Due to hostile and rigorous environment, the copper pipe is subject to pits occurring on the external surface of the pipe. It is crucial and highly demanded to noninvasively detect and evaluate this flaw which has posed a severe threat to integrity of copper pipes. In light of the advantages of gradient-field pulsed eddy current technique (GPEC), this paper intensively investigates the detection and evaluation of subsurface pits in copper pipes via GPEC. A GPEC probe consisting of a bobbin-type excitation coil and array of magnetic sensors has been proposed for efficient pipe inspection. A new feature extracted from the differential signal of gradient-field is utilized for localization and assessment of pits distributing circumferentially and axially. Through a series of experiments, it can be found that the subsurface pit of ixQ.imm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in diameterxdepth can be localized and quantitatively evaluated by using GPEC which is also found advantageous over conventional pulsed eddy current technique (PEC) in terms of higher efficiency and sensitivity to subsurface pits in copper pipes.

articleTitle: Laser-based ultrasonic detection by using all-fiber adaptive fiber Bragg grating sensors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel nondestructive testing (NDT) method based on laser ultrasonic technology and fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensors. A FBG sensor is employed as discrete sensing elements to detect the ultrasonic generated by pulsed laser. An all-fiber and adaptive acousto-ultrasonic (AU) monitoring system for the dynamic detection of impact damage is developed for the present work. A tunable distributed feedback semiconductor laser is used to track AU frequencies as a demodulation scheme. To continuously lock the laser wavelength to the middle-reflection wavelength of FBG, a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) device is integrated with the signals from the photodetector in a feedback loop, thus stabilizing the operating points against quasi-state perturbations such as temperature and vibration, while the high frequency dynamic strain shifts the FBG reflection spectral profiles. We demonstrate the all-fiber adaptive AU demodulating system that has the sensing capability to monitor the high frequency AU signals using FBG that is glued on a loaded aluminum plate.

articleTitle: A pre-calculation beamformer design based on FPGA for ultrasound SA imaging
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The previous studies of real-time imaging process using directly delay calculation design on FPGA, because the limited number of memory on chip. In this paper, to achieve higher frequency, a look-up table which carries the distance information has been introduced in. As the operation frequency of memory on Field-programmable gate array (FPGA) can reach to as high as 400MHz, which is much higher than directly calculation. After the design of hardware language and compile, the performance of this beamformer was assessed on an Altera Stratix IV FPGA. The final performance shows the highest frequency is 300MHz. Experiment on total focus method SA imaging processing with 64 channels, our FPGA-based SA beamformer can achieve 32 frames per second (fps) processing (100MHz sample frequency, 16 bits resolution, frame size 256×256 pixels). According the experimental result, the beamformer can be used as real-time ultrasound processor modules.

articleTitle: Damage assessment of real-size T-beam from deficient prestressed concrete bridge using ultrasonic coda waves
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: We present a nondestructive evaluation method, based on ultrasonic coda wave interferometry measurement with applied small successive stress change (~10kPa to ~140kPa) under a four-point bending test, to assess the damage level of a real-size T-beam from a deficient prestressed concrete bridge. The acousto-elasticity coefficient is 4.17× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>MPa<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> subject to compressional force, in associate with -17×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>MPa<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> subject to tensile force. The acousto-elasticity coefficient which is highly relevant to damage level, indicate the intense damage of mechanical properties of the tested T-beam.

articleTitle: Multi-aperture focus ultrasonic imaging technique based on virtual source
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-aperture synthetic focusing technique based on virtual source is studied, which improves the lateral resolution and depth of the ultrasonic imaging with respect to the single array dynamic synthetic aperture focusing technique (SAFT). It only needs to store the N numbers data for the A scan line, and the complexity of the algorithm is greatly reduced compared with the full focus technology (TFM) with the maintenance of image quality. Using Field II simulation and Multi2000 device experiment results show that compared with the single element dynamic synthetic aperture technology, virtual source multi-aperture synthetic focusing ultrasonic technique (VS-MSAFT) effectively improves the lateral resolution and depth of permeation, furthermore to improve the quality of ultrasound imaging.

articleTitle: Non-destructive detection of TVB-N content in fresh pork based on hyperspectral imaging technology
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Non-destructive detection of total volatile basic-nitrogen (TVB-N) content in fresh pork based on hyperspectral imaging (HSI) technology was evaluated. In order to build a firm hyperspectral calibration model of TVB-N content in fresh pork, discussion about the impacts of different data processing methods(sample set partitioning, characteristic wavelength selection, and so on)on the predictive results was done. The results showed that, the best partial least square regression (PLSR) calibration model established with the whole spectral range was that using concentration gradient (CG) to partition samples, and using normalize combined with mean center(MC) to preprocess the spectral, resulting in R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cv</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.9508 and R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.9357, RMSECV of 1.3042 and RMSEP of 1.5130. After 49 optimal wavelengths were selected by using competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) algorithm, 93.5% data redundancy was got rid of and the precision of PLSR model which was established using the selected 49 wavelengths was improved. It increased R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>v<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 0.9640, R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 0.9531, and decreased RMSECV to 1.1151, RMSEP to 1.2885. All the results showed that hyperspectral imaging technology is a powerful technique to detect the TVB-N content in fresh pork non-destructively.

Index Terms: Root Mean Square Error Of Prediction

articleTitle: Repeatability study of magnetic domain wall behaviors for stress characterization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Magnetic domain behaviors directly characterize the macroscopic properties of ferromagnetic material, the understanding of domain wall dynamic is a way to explain the characteristics of magnetization process and performance of material. This paper presents the repeatability study of domain wall behavior for stress characterization. A high grain-oriented (HGO) electric steel is employed for domain textures observation using magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) microscopy. Three conditions of different stress load, magnetic disturbance and time are considered for the domain wall repeatability analysis. The experimental results indicate that domain behavior can be applied for strain measurement.

articleTitle: The impact of elastic anisotropy on ultrasonic inspection and materials characterization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This paper addresses the questions: “Of what importance is elastic anisotropy in ultrasonic inspection and materials characterization? Is anisotropy something NDT professionals should be aware of, and are they likely to encounter it in their activities?” The first part of the paper describes the principal types of anisotropic materials. The second part sketches some of the basic ideas that come up in the treatment of elastic wave propagation in anisotropic solids. The third part deals with a number of applications.

articleTitle: Detection of interlayer delamination in W monoblock of ITER divertors via electromagnetic acoustic transduction
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The W monoblock is one of the key components in divertors of the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER). During fabrication, it is prone to interlayer delamination posing a severe threat to integrity of diverters and safe operation of ITER. This opens up the research of efficient nondestructive evaluation techniques for quality assessment of W monoblock. In this paper, electromagnetic acoustic transduction with full-circumference radial excitation (FREM-EMAT) for detection of interlayer delamination in W monoblock has been intensively investigated via simulations and experiments. The probe parameters including the distance between permanent magnets, magnet type and height of excitation coil, etc and their influence on the transduction efficiency and testing signals are analyzed through semi-analytical modeling. Following this, a series of experiments have been carried out for detection of simulated interlayer delamination in W monoblocks via FREM-EMAT. It can be seen from the results that FREM-EMAT is capable of efficiently detecting the interlayer delamination with the diameter of 1mm in W monoblock, which fulfills the engineering requirement.

articleTitle: Relative reliability-guided phase unwrapping algorithm based on region partition and application on train wheel profilometry
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, a relative reliability-guided phase unwrapping algorithm based on region partition is proposed, the designing and processing of the algorithm is discussed. Firstly, the wrapped phase map in profilometry is divided into different regions to reduce the spread of noise. Secondly, the relative reliability of adjacent pixels is used to guide the path of phase unwrapping in different regions. Finally, the adjacent regions are integrated by solving the extreme value of the weighted edge continuous cost function. Simulation data and experiment on train wheel three-dimension (3-D) measurement shows that the proposed algorithm can effectively avoid the phenomenon of stretching, which caused by noise diffusion, and has a better accuracy and a better flaw detection capability than the quality map guided algorithm.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis of rolling element bearings based on FDK and Hilbert spectrum
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach based on a combination of the Hilbert spectrum and frequency domain kurtosis (FDK) is presented for diagnosing faults in rolling element bearings. This method not only can filter out noisy signals, but also detect and characterize fault components in a signal. By using the Hilbert transform to envelope demodulation and removal of noise in frequency components, the fault feature information in a low frequency envelope signal can be obtained. Then, FDK is used to analyze the envelope signal. According to the FDK results, the scope of the filter band can be determined and the vibration signal can be filtered. The proposed method is especially suited for detecting the fault characteristic frequency of rotating machinery. Experiments are conducted on a simulator to demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the method is advantageous for extracting fault signals and reducing the influence of interfering components in the background noise.

articleTitle: Phased array ultrasonic probe simulation and designing for railway axle inspection
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: When the solid axle is detected by the conventional ultrasonic probes, the inspecting coverage of axle is very limited, especially for the press-fit part of axle where the signal-to-noise ratio of detection is very low, and the echoes are difficult to distinguish, which easily leads to false judgment or missing judgment. In view of this phenomenon, a kind of dedicated phased array ultrasonic probe is introduced in this paper. Based on the advantages of phased array ultrasonic technology, relative theoretical analysis and simulation comparison are conducted. Finally, this probe is proved to have superior detection ability of railway axle inspection by comparison test.

articleTitle: A study of the residual stress of rail detection and regulation technology
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Rail is a main part of railway track. Its reliability relates to the national economy and people's livelihood. The fracture of rail will lead to disastrous consequences. This article mainly introduces the residual stress of rail detection and regulation technology, completes the relevant tensile experiments and rail experiments, analyses the results and the function of regulation. Eventually, an effective way to detect and reduce the residual stress of rail is found.

articleTitle: Experiment research and correction model building on radiation thermometry for nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Radiation thermometry is one of the most important technical means in routine temperature patrol of critical component identification(CCI) in nuclear power plant(NPP). Based on the status of complicated thermometry environment, and measurement process being difficult to reach ideal state, this paper focuses on the theory and experiment analysis of emissivity on measured surface, thermometry distance, environment temperature etc. According to experiments and referring the emissivity impact correction and environment radiation error correction in classical brightness theory, this paper build correction model on radiation thermometry for nuclear power plant(NPP). Experiments proved that by means of correcting the initial results through correction model on radiation thermometry, the temperature precision of on-site thermometry can be greatly increased.

articleTitle: Keynote Speech 1: ASNT's vision on certification of NDT personnel with respect to current and future technologies
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: It is a great honor to be invited here to share thoughts on the subject of “ASNT's vision on Certification of NDT Personnel with respect to current and future technologies.” My professional career mirrors this title. Most of you are experienced in multiple NDT methods, while I have only one method: infrared thermography. The name “Infrared Thermography” is a bit misleading because it refers specifically to the operation of infrared cameras. A better description is thermal and spectral analysis because infrared testing is fundamentally about the behavior of infrared radiation in materials. Twenty-five years ago. Infrared thermography was classically thought of as condition monitoring for electrical power distribution systems. Today, the category has matured into a high tech method for examining aerospace composite materials and there is no clear distinction between condition monitoring and nondestructive testing.
